senses.gloss:
calaliṅga
(‘movable लिङ्ग’)
------------------------------------------
Śivaliṅgas or emblems of शिव, the third deity of the Hindu Trinity, are of two types: acalaliṅgas and calaliṅgas. The former are immovable or fixed, whereas the latter are movable or portable. Stone liṅgas fixed in temples belong to the former category.
The calaliṅgas are of various types: mṛṇmaya (made of earth or clay), lohaja (prepared out of metal), ratnaja (shaped out of precious stones), dāruja (carved out of wood), śailaja (made of stone) and kṣaṇika-liṅgas (those prepared temporarily for the occasion and disposed off, like the ones made out of riverside clay or cooked rice).
White clay gathered from pure places such as hilltops or river-beds is recommended for mṛṇmayaliṅgas. The lohaja liṅgas are generally cast from metals like gold, silver or copper. The ratnaja variety is shaped out of precious stones like pearls, coral, topaz or emerald. The timber of trees like शमी (Prosposis spicegera), madhuka (Bassis latifolia), अर्जुन (Termi-nalia अर्जुन) pippala (Ficus religiosa) or udumbara (Ficus glomerata) is recommended for dāruliṅgas. The śailaja or stone liṅgas are generally worn on the body by the followers of Śaiva cults like the liṅgāyats. The kṣaṇika liṅgas are shaped out of riverside sand or clay, uncooked or cooked rice, cowdung, butter, sandal paste, flour or jaggery. They are made for the occasion and then disposed off, soon after the worship is over.
Worship of different kinds of liṅgas confers different results. For instance, that of gold लिङ्ग gives wealth; that of cooked rice, plenty of ड़ोओद्; that of cowdung, freedom from diseases.
Baked clay liṅgas are used for ābhicārika purposes, i.e., for harming others through black magic.
See also ACALALIṄGA, ŚIVA and ŚIVALIṄGA.
